Author: Babylon Labs

Date: 14-10-26

Simple Summary

This proposal requests the activation of native BTC as collateral on Aave V4 via the Trustless Bitcoin Vaults (TBV) protocol. The integration deploys two new Aave V4 Spokes, the Babylon Spoke and the BTC Vault Swap Spoke, and lists native BTC as the sole collateral asset of the Babylon Spoke. The first use case is borrowing stablecoins against native BTC. Risk parameters for both Spokes will be provided by Aave’s risk service providers.

In TBV, a depositor locks BTC in a Taproot UTXO on Bitcoin Network. Redemption is governed by on-chain rules (e.g., the depositor repaid their loan) and settles directly to a Bitcoin UTXO controlled by the redeeming party. The deposited BTC is not wrapped, bridged or held by a custodian.

Following the passed Temperature Check on this integration, the ARFC extends
that scope to the integration with the Aave V4 Hub and Spoke architecture, the
BTC vault lifecycle and its trust assumptions, liquidation and arbitrage
mechanics, value accrual, and governance.

Context

Babylon

Babylon was started in 2022 by Stanford University Professor David Tse and Dr. Fisher Yu, with a vision of a Bitcoin-backed crypto economy built on trustless protocols that unlock Bitcoin’s productivity without bridges, wrappers, or custodians.

The project is best known for the Bitcoin staking protocol, which lets BTC holders stake their BTC to secure other chains and rollups to provide economic security and earn staking rewards. The protocol is fully self-custodial: BTC never leaves Bitcoin and is not held by a bridge, wrapper, or signer set. Since the protocol’s launch in August 2024, the protocol has activated over 100,000 BTC cumulatively, reached a peak TVL of 72,000 BTC, and currently holds ~40,772 BTC (approximately $3.37B) staked.

The success of Bitcoin staking demonstrated that BTC holders seek trustless and native ways to put their Bitcoin to work. This motivated the development of Trustless Bitcoin Vaults (TBV), which extends the same trustless and self-custodial principles to general DeFi participation, and is the subject of this proposal.

The Babylon project is backed by approximately $110M+ to date from a16z, Paradigm, Polychain, Hack VC and others.

Trustless Bitcoin Vaults (TBV)

Trustless Bitcoin Vaults (TBV) allows anyone to use their native bitcoins as collateral in supported on-chain applications, without transferring custody to any trusted third party.

TBV achieves this by locking BTC on Bitcoin inside a Taproot script. The conditions under which it can be moved are enforced cryptographically: redemption requires a valid zero-knowledge proof of an event on the host chain (e.g. Ethereum Mainnet), and any attempt to claim BTC without a valid proof can be challenged and stopped by an eligible challenger during a fraud-proof window. The depositor can act as a challenger themselves by operating their own vault provider, so they need not trust any third party to secure their BTC.

Spending conditions are encoded in the Taproot script and pre-authorized by all vault participants, including the depositor. The protocol itself is governed by zero-knowledge proofs through a challenge-based procedure, efficiently enabled by the BaBe protocol, and redemption is native to Bitcoin. The locked BTC moves to a recipient designated by the vault’s spending conditions, which reference events on the host chain.

TBV can be integrated with any application on any supported host chain. Ethereum is the first supported host chain and the one this integration is built on. When BTC is locked in a Taproot script, a corresponding collateral record is created on Ethereum. Each application integration builds on it, optionally via an adapter layer that exposes it through the application’s interface. For the Aave V4 integration, since Aave V4 only accepts ERC-20 tokens as collateral, the adapter contracts represent BTCVaults 1:1 as a transfer-restricted ERC-20 representation token. The full component set is detailed in Architecture Overview.

TBV is built on BaBe (eprint 2026/065), peer-reviewed cryptographic research (to appear in CCS 2026, a top security conference) developed jointly by Babylon Labs and UC Berkeley. BaBe makes SNARK proof verification on Bitcoin approximately 1000x cheaper than prior approaches, making trustless Bitcoin DeFi practical at scale.

Motivation

The Aave V4 integration with Babylon Trustless Bitcoin Vaults protocol enables onboarding of non-custodial native BTC collateral on Aave. Depositors can borrow allowed loan assets against this collateral, with no third-party custodian, signer consortium, or threshold-signature group holding the underlying BTC.

The BTC Vault Swap Spoke enables permissionless liquidation on Aave despite the underlying collateral settling natively on Bitcoin. Any liquidator can settle the position by receiving wrapped BTC for a small premium, while arbitrageurs purchase the escrowed vaults and handle the BTC-side redemption. Mechanism described in Specification.

Every escrowed BTCVault is backed by wrapped BTC borrowed from the Hub, creating new borrow demand for that asset. At launch this is WBTC, Aave’s largest BTC reserve and presently underutilized on the borrow side; the integration can use any other wrapped BTC.

Native BTC as collateral on Aave V4 also serves as a composable primitive for the broader BTC DeFi ecosystem. Other projects can build new BTC-collateralized products on top, extending Aave’s reach into BTC-native DeFi.

Specification

Architecture Overview

The TBV deployment on Ethereum consists of protocol contracts and application contracts. A BTCVault is the protocol’s core primitive, BTC locked in a UTXO on Bitcoin, secured by its pre-signed transaction graph. On Ethereum, each BTCVault is represented by a collateral record carrying its amount, its depositor, its participant set, and its lifecycle state. The protocol contracts track collateral records and enforce the vault lifecycle, from creation through activation to redemption.

The application contracts define how BTCVaults are used inside the integrated application, in this case as collateral for Aave V4 Babylon Spoke. The Aave application layer consists of the adapter contracts, the two new Spokes, and the collateral representation token. Depositors supply their BTCVaults and manage their positions through the adapter, and liquidators call it to liquidate unhealthy positions. The Babylon Spoke is a variant of the standard Aave V4 Spoke, written by Aave Labs and maintained in the Aave V4 repository (Babylon Spoke), while the BTC Vault Swap Spoke introduces custom Spoke code.

Babylon Spoke

On the Babylon Spoke, depositors borrow against native BTC, the Spoke’s only collateral asset, drawing the borrowed assets from an Aave V4 Hub.

The Spoke differs from the standard Spoke in liquidation and collateral registration only. Only the Babylon Aave V4 adapter, configured as the Spoke’s liquidation manager, can liquidate on the Spoke. The standard liquidation entry point is disabled. Each liquidation call targets one BTCVault. The adapter passes the BTCVault’s amount to the Spoke as the maximum collateral to remove, and the Spoke repays only as much debt as that amount covers at the liquidation bonus, instead of repaying toward a target health factor. The Spoke charges no liquidation fee and applies no dust threshold, so the liquidator receives all the collateral removed. A position can use only the native BTC reserve as collateral.

The Spoke exposes the same set of risk parameters as a standard Aave V4 Spoke, with values configured for this Spoke. Because the collateral token cannot be transferred, some parameters are fixed: native BTC is collateral only and non-borrowable, the liquidation fee is zero, and receiving shares on liquidation is disabled. The target health factor has been removed, as each liquidation call seizes a single BTCVault and the liquidator repeats the call until the position is healthy.

A depositor locks BTC on Bitcoin, creating a BTCVault, and supplies it through the adapter. The adapter exposes the standard position-management actions, and the liquidation (both permissionless and permissioned) entry points.

Native BTC Collateral Representation

Aave V4 accepts only ERC-20 tokens as collateral. Native BTC collateral is therefore represented by an ERC-20 token with transfer restrictions. The token is an internal accounting unit, not a BTC wrapper, it cannot be transferred between users, traded, or held anywhere outside the integration.

The token has 8 decimals, matching Bitcoin’s satoshi denomination. Transfers are allowed only between the integration’s Aave contracts, a fixed allowlist made up of the Aave V4 Hub, the adapter contract, and the per-user position proxy contracts that hold each depositor’s position.

There are no risk parameters to configure for this token. The token contract is not upgradeable and has no admin. Its decimals, transfer restrictions, and the Hub and adapter addresses are set at deployment and cannot be changed.

Mint and burn are restricted to the adapter contract. The token is minted at BTCVault activation, directly into the depositor’s position, and burned when a vault leaves a position, whether withdrawn by the depositor or seized in liquidation. No other mint or burn path exists. By design, total supply equals the BTC locked in active positions.

BTC Vault Swap Spoke

A custom Spoke for post-liquidation BTC collateral settlement.

When a position is liquidated by a permissionless liquidator, the liquidator swaps the acquired BTCVaults through this Spoke for wrapped BTC, at the oracle rate minus a sell discount. The wrapped BTC is a BTC-denominated ERC-20 fixed when the Spoke is deployed, WBTC at launch. It is drawn from an Aave V4 Hub and held as interest-accruing debt against the escrowed BTCVaults. Arbitrageurs, a permissioned set with redemption rights, later buy individual escrowed BTCVaults by repaying that debt (principal plus accrued interest) and redeem the BTC on Bitcoin.

The Spoke exists because BTC redemption is restricted to pre-committed actors in each BTCVault’s Taproot script and takes multiple days through the claim challenge window. Decoupling liquidation timing from BTC redemption lets permissionless liquidators settle in wrapped BTC immediately while arbitrageurs handle redemption on Bitcoin’s timeline.

The BTC Vault Swap Spoke moves Hub funds in two ways. The first is the wrapped BTC draw and repayment described above. The second is the deficit path, used when an escrowed BTCVault’s value no longer covers its Hub debt. The BTCVault stays purchasable at its current value. The arbitrageur repays the Hub debt, capped at the BTCVault’s value less a reserved arbitrageur margin. Any shortfall is reported to the Hub as a deficit in the same transaction.

The BTC Vault Swap Spoke has 3 configurable parameters: the sell discount, the minimum profit reserved for the arbitrageur, and the fee recipient.

Governance, Control & Pause States

Both Spokes (the Babylon Spoke and the BTC Vault Swap Spoke) are governed by Aave DAO. Aave DAO lists the collateral asset and the borrowable assets, and sets the Spoke configuration parameters, including supply and borrow caps, interest rate strategy, liquidation parameters, and oracle configuration. It can also freeze or pause each listed asset individually, where freezing stops new supply and borrowing while pausing stops all activity for that asset. Any Hub used for drawing liquidity for these Spokes will also be governed by Aave DAO. A separate role for configuring the BTC Vault Swap Spoke is held by a 2-of-3 multisig of Llama Risk, Babylon Labs, and Aave Labs.

The Babylon TBV contracts are governed by Babylon governance representatives. They manage the TBV protocol configuration and the actor sets, and hold pause and freeze controls over the TBV contracts. A freeze blocks new vault creations and new borrows, while all exit paths keep working. A pause additionally stops the exit paths and is reserved for emergencies. All governance actions on the TBV contracts execute through a public timelock with advance on-chain notice.

Vault Lifecycle & Position Management

Vault Creation

The TBV protocol is trustless. BTCVault creation and redemption need a set of actors that coordinate with each other. The protocol defines three types of actors.

  • Vault Provider. An infrastructure operator appointed by the depositor. It sets up and redeems the BTCVault for that depositor and challenges fraudulent claims. The depositor can run it themselves.
  • Application Vault Keepers. An application-specific set of actors with claim and challenge rights over that application’s BTCVaults. On Aave V4, they claim BTCVaults that have been liquidated and act as the arbitrageurs.
  • Universal Challengers. A global set of actors. They can challenge bad claims on any BTCVault, across every application.

The depositor locks BTC in a Taproot output on Bitcoin and submits a creation request on Ethereum. The vault provider, every application vault keeper, and every universal challenger must acknowledge the request and pre-sign the vault’s transaction graph, the fixed set of Bitcoin transactions through which the locked BTC can ever move. Acknowledgments are given only after the locked BTC is confirmed on Bitcoin. By design, nothing outside the pre-signed graph can spend the vault.

Once all acknowledgments are in, the depositor activates the vault by revealing a secret on Ethereum. If the depositor does not activate, or any actor fails to acknowledge, the request expires and the depositor reclaims the locked BTC unilaterally through a timelocked refund. By design, collateral can never exist without locked BTC behind it. On activation, the BTCVault enters the depositor’s Aave position, and from there the position is managed through the adapter.

Position Management

Every position action goes through the adapter. The depositor never interacts with the Babylon Spoke directly.

Borrowing and repaying follow standard Aave mechanics. On top of Aave interest, the adapter can charge a Babylon interest fee, a percentage of the borrower’s base Aave interest, collected on repayment. Collateral handling is custom, tailored to BTCVaults. A position can hold several BTCVaults. Each one is a single locked Bitcoin UTXO, so collateral moves in whole BTCVaults and never in part. The Babylon Spoke sees only the position’s total collateral amount, while the adapter tracks which BTCVaults make it up. The depositor adds collateral by activating additional BTCVaults into the position and withdraws whole BTCVaults while the position’s health factor stays at or above liquidation threshold. A borrower with multiple BTCVaults can set the order in which a liquidation seizes them.

Vault Redemption

A BTCVault is redeemed when application logic on Ethereum releases it. In the Aave V4 integration this happens in two cases. The borrower withdraws any subset of their BTCVaults while the position stays healthy, or the vault is liquidated and leaves through the liquidation flow. The application contracts define and enforce these rules on Ethereum. Each redemption emits an event naming the BTC keys authorized to claim the vault on Bitcoin.

The claim settles on Bitcoin. Only actors pre-committed in the vault’s Taproot script can claim, and the depositor is always one of them. The authorized claimer posts a Claim backed by a zero-knowledge proof of the Ethereum redemption event. If the proof is invalid, any challenger can stop the Claim during the claim challenge window. Challengers are all of the vault’s participants, the vault provider, every application vault keeper, and every universal challenger. By design, a challenge cannot block a valid claim. After the window passes, the BTC settles to the authorized key. The full timeline from redemption to settlement is multiple days, set by the claim challenge window.

Liquidation

Once a position’s health factor drops below liquidation threshold, anyone can liquidate it through the adapter, one BTCVault at a time. The adapter seizes the first BTCVault in the order the borrower set in advance. The liquidator repays the position’s debt asset. The collateral the Spoke removes is priced at the standard Aave liquidation bonus for the position’s health factor at entry. The Spoke stops once the collateral owed for the repaid debt reaches the BTCVault’s amount. The adapter refunds any repayment input the Spoke did not spend. A position holding several BTCVaults is liquidated through repeated calls. Each call checks the health factor again.

Liquidation always seizes whole BTCVaults. If the borrower’s entire debt is repaid before the BTCVault’s amount is consumed, the liquidator still receives the whole BTCVault and pays the borrower for the remainder in wrapped BTC (WBTC at launch) at the same liquidation-bonus discount. The borrower therefore receives that portion as discounted wrapped BTC instead of native BTC. The liquidator must hold the wrapped BTC and sets a cap on the total it can be charged.

Liquidation runs through two paths (permissioned and permissionless). In the permissioned path, an application vault keeper, which holds redemption rights over the vault, liquidates the position and redeems the seized BTCVault to its own BTC key. No external liquidity is involved.

In the permissionless path, anyone can liquidate. Because redemption is restricted to the pre-committed actors in each BTCVault’s Taproot script, these liquidators cannot redeem the BTCVaults they seize, so the integration introduces liquidation liquidity providers. A venue swaps the seized BTCVaults for a fungible asset immediately, instead of after the multi-day Bitcoin settlement.

The BTC Vault Swap Spoke is the first such venue. It purchases the seized BTCVaults from the liquidator for wrapped BTC drawn as debt from an Aave V4 Hub in the same transaction and holds them in escrow for the arbitrageurs to buy and redeem, as described in Architecture Overview. Additional venues can be added if scale requires.

Aave DAO Value Accrual

On the Babylon Spoke, borrowers pay standard borrow interest on every asset drawn from the Hub, exactly as on any other Spoke. On the BTC Vault Swap Spoke, escrowed BTCVaults accrue wrapped BTC borrow interest to the Hub until an arbitrageur repays the draw. This adds borrow demand on whichever wrapped BTC the integration uses, WBTC at launch, Aave’s largest wrapped BTC reserve and presently underutilized on the borrow side.

Native BTC as collateral on Aave V4 also serves as a composable primitive for the broader BTC DeFi ecosystem. Other projects can build new BTC-collateralized products on top, extending Aave’s reach into BTC-native DeFi.

Revenue Sharing

This proposal includes revenue sharing between Aave DAO and Babylon Foundation.
Babylon Foundation is responsible for the incentive arrangements supporting the
integration, such as borrower incentives and strategic integrations. These do
not guarantee borrower demand, revenue, token purchases or returns.

Revenue sharing applies only to Qualifying Revenue, the protocol-level fees
listed below, not all interest paid by borrowers:

  • The Aave Hub’s Liquidity Fee on interest paid by Babylon Spoke borrowers.
  • Liquidation fees charged through the adapter and the BTC Vault Swap Spoke.

The first $500,000 of Qualifying Revenue in each year from launch goes entirely
to Aave DAO. Above that, each band’s split applies only to the revenue within
that band, with distributions made monthly.

The token purchase allocation funds open-market purchases of AAVE (85%) and
BABY (15%), with purchased tokens allocated equally to Aave DAO and
Babylon Foundation.

Audits & Formal Verification

Security audit engagements have been completed across five components, the btc-vault, the vault provers, the smart contracts, the web services, and BaBe. Six firms were engaged, with overlapping scopes so that every component is covered by at least two independent reviews. Coinspect additionally performed a pre-audit of the full protocol before the main engagements. Runtime Verification performed formal verification of the smart contracts. Babylon is running a re-audit of the finalized changes before mainnet deployment, carried out by Coinspect, ABDK and Zellic. The follow-up reports will be shared once finalized.

Next Steps

  1. Seek community feedback and risk analysis
  2. If community consensus is reached, raise to Snapshot.
  3. If the Snapshot outcome is positive, submit an AIP, with full risk parameters included, for on-chain governance approval.

Acknowledgments are given only after the locked BTC is confirmed on Bitcoin. By design, nothing outside the pre-signed graph can spend the vault.

Once all acknowledgments are in, the depositor activates the vault by revealing a secret on Ethereum. If the depositor does not activate, or any actor fails to acknowledge, the request expires and the depositor reclaims the locked BTC unilaterally through a timelocked refund. By design, collateral can never exist without locked BTC behind it. On activation, the BTCVault enters the depositor’s Aave position, and from there the position is managed through the adapter.

Position Management

Every position action goes through the adapter. The depositor never interacts with the Babylon Spoke directly.

Borrowing and repaying follow standard Aave mechanics. On top of Aave interest, the adapter can charge a Babylon interest fee, a percentage of the borrower’s base Aave interest, collected on repayment. Collateral handling is custom, tailored to BTCVaults. A position can hold several BTCVaults. Each one is a single locked Bitcoin UTXO, so collateral moves in whole BTCVaults and never in part. The Babylon Spoke sees only the position’s total collateral amount, while the adapter tracks which BTCVaults make it up. The depositor adds collateral by activating additional BTCVaults into the position and withdraws whole BTCVaults while the position’s health factor stays at or above liquidation threshold. A borrower with multiple BTCVaults can set the order in which a liquidation seizes them.

Vault Redemption

A BTCVault is redeemed when application logic on Ethereum releases it. In the Aave V4 integration this happens in two cases. The borrower withdraws any subset of their BTCVaults while the position stays healthy, or the vault is liquidated and leaves through the liquidation flow. The application contracts define and enforce these rules on Ethereum. Each redemption emits an event naming the BTC keys authorized to claim the vault on Bitcoin.

The claim settles on Bitcoin. Only actors pre-committed in the vault’s Taproot script can claim, and the depositor is always one of them. The authorized claimer posts a Claim backed by a zero-knowledge proof of the Ethereum redemption event. If the proof is invalid, any challenger can stop the Claim during the claim challenge window. Challengers are all of the vault’s participants, the vault provider, every application vault keeper, and every universal challenger. By design, a challenge cannot block a valid claim. After the window passes, the BTC settles to the authorized key. The full timeline from redemption to settlement is multiple days, set by the claim challenge window.

Liquidation

Once a position’s health factor drops below liquidation threshold, anyone can liquidate it through the adapter, one BTCVault at a time. The adapter seizes the first BTCVault in the order the borrower set in advance. The liquidator repays the position’s debt asset. The collateral the Spoke removes is priced at the standard Aave liquidation bonus for the position’s health factor at entry. The Spoke stops once the collateral owed for the repaid debt reaches the BTCVault’s amount. The adapter refunds any repayment input the Spoke did not spend. A position holding several BTCVaults is liquidated through repeated calls. Each call checks the health factor again.

Liquidation always seizes whole BTCVaults. If the borrower’s entire debt is repaid before the BTCVault’s amount is consumed, the liquidator still receives the whole BTCVault and pays the borrower for the remainder in wrapped BTC (WBTC at launch) at the same liquidation-bonus discount. The borrower therefore receives that portion as discounted wrapped BTC instead of native BTC. The liquidator must hold the wrapped BTC and sets a cap on the total it can be charged.

Liquidation runs through two paths (permissioned and permissionless). In the permissioned path, an application vault keeper, which holds redemption rights over the vault, liquidates the position and redeems the seized BTCVault to its own BTC key. No external liquidity is involved.

In the permissionless path, anyone can liquidate. Because redemption is restricted to the pre-committed actors in each BTCVault’s Taproot script, these liquidators cannot redeem the BTCVaults they seize, so the integration introduces liquidation liquidity providers. A venue swaps the seized BTCVaults for a fungible asset immediately, instead of after the multi-day Bitcoin settlement.

The BTC Vault Swap Spoke is the first such venue. It purchases the seized BTCVaults from the liquidator for wrapped BTC drawn as debt from an Aave V4 Hub in the same transaction and holds them in escrow for the arbitrageurs to buy and redeem, as described in Architecture Overview. Additional venues can be added if scale requires.

Aave DAO Value Accrual

On the Babylon Spoke, borrowers pay standard borrow interest on every asset drawn from the Hub, exactly as on any other Spoke. On the BTC Vault Swap Spoke, escrowed BTCVaults accrue wrapped BTC borrow interest to the Hub until an arbitrageur repays the draw. This adds borrow demand on whichever wrapped BTC the integration uses, WBTC at launch, Aave’s largest wrapped BTC reserve and presently underutilized on the borrow side.

Native BTC as collateral on Aave V4 also serves as a composable primitive for the broader BTC DeFi ecosystem. Other projects can build new BTC-collateralized products on top, extending Aave’s reach into BTC-native DeFi.

Revenue Sharing

This proposal includes revenue sharing between Aave DAO and Babylon Foundation.
Babylon Foundation is responsible for the incentive arrangements supporting the
integration, such as borrower incentives and strategic integrations. These do
not guarantee borrower demand, revenue, token purchases or returns.

Revenue sharing applies only to Qualifying Revenue, the protocol-level fees
listed below, not all interest paid by borrowers:

  • The Aave Hub’s Liquidity Fee on interest paid by Babylon Spoke borrowers.
  • Liquidation fees charged through the adapter and the BTC Vault Swap Spoke.

The first $500,000 of Qualifying Revenue in each year from launch goes entirely
to Aave DAO. Above that, each band’s split applies only to the revenue within
that band, with distributions made monthly.

The token purchase allocation funds open-market purchases of AAVE (85%) and
BABY (15%), with purchased tokens allocated equally to Aave DAO and
Babylon Foundation.

Annual revenue band Aave DAO Babylon Token purchase allocation
First $500,000 100% 0% 0%
$500,000–$2 million 78% 18% 4%
$2 million–$4 million 72.5% 22.5% 5%
$4 million–$6 million 67% 27% 6%
Above $6 million 61.5% 31.5% 7%

Audits & Formal Verification

Security audit engagements have been completed across five components, the btc-vault, the vault provers, the smart contracts, the web services, and BaBe. Six firms were engaged, with overlapping scopes so that every component is covered by at least two independent reviews. Coinspect additionally performed a pre-audit of the full protocol before the main engagements. Runtime Verification performed formal verification of the smart contracts. Babylon is running a re-audit of the finalized changes before mainnet deployment, carried out by Coinspect, ABDK and Zellic. The follow-up reports will be shared once finalized.

  2. If community consensus is reached, raise to Snapshot.
  3. If the Snapshot outcome is positive, submit an AIP, with full risk parameters included, for on-chain governance approval.

title: [Direct-to-AIP] Asset Listing - USDG Arbitrum
author: @TokenLogic
created: 2026-10-08

Summary

This publication proposes to onboard USDG as a supported asset on the Aave V3 Arbitrum Instance.

USDG would join the instance as a borrowable stablecoin, giving Arbitrum users another option to supply and borrow.

Motivation

USDG is a stablecoin issued by Paxos. According to Paxos documentation, USDG on Arbitrum is deployed through LayerZero OFT from Ethereum.

USDG is listed on Aave V3 Ethereum Core, Aave V3 X Layer, Aave V3 Ink (Tydro), and Aave V4 Ethereum through the Core Hub and the Global Dollar Hub, with collateral use disabled in each market. USDG supply on Aave is growing quickly, rising from $94.1M to $123.2M over the last 90 days, which makes USDG a strong candidate stablecoin for the Aave V3 Arbitrum Instance.

On Aave V3 Arbitrum, stablecoin liquidity is concentrated in the USDC and USD₮0 reserves, both of which run at high utilisation, while the other stablecoin reserves on the instance are frozen or small.

Onboarding USDG to Aave V3 Arbitrum would:

  • Provide an additional borrowable stablecoin alongside USDC and USD₮0.
  • Add borrowing capacity without increasing the instance’s collateral risk, as USDG would not be active as collateral.
  • Extend USDG’s presence on Aave to Arbitrum, in line with its listings on other Aave markets.

The listing would bring a Paxos-issued stablecoin to Arbitrum and give USDG holders on the network a market to supply into.

Specification

USDG Contract Address

The address above represents Paxos’s USDG deployment on Arbitrum.

Proposed Market Configuration

We propose initially configuring USDG with the following parameters, subject to final recommendations from Aave Risk Service Providers.

Parameter Value
Asset USDG
Isolation Mode No
Borrowable Yes
Collateral Enabled No
Supply Cap 30,000,000
Borrow Cap 27,600,000
Debt Ceiling -
LTV 0.00%
LT 0.00%
Liquidation Bonus 0.00%
Liquidation Protocol Fee 10%
Variable Base 0.00%
Variable Slope 1 4.00%
Variable Slope 2 30.00%
Uoptimal 90.00%
Reserve Factor 10%
Stable Borrowing Disabled
Flashloanable Yes
Siloed Borrowing No
Borrowable in Isolation Yes
eModes -

The proposed configuration excludes USDG from collateral use, consistent with its listings on the other Aave instances. It uses the same interest rate curve as the USDC reserve on Aave V3 Arbitrum and sets a 10% reserve factor, matching USDC and USD₮0 on Arbitrum and USDG on X Layer and Ink.

We consider USDG’s secondary-market liquidity on Arbitrum, concentrated in the Fluid USDG/USDC pool, sufficient for an initial listing.

Final onboarding parameters remain subject to review and recommendations from Aave’s Risk Service Providers.

Oracle

A Chainlink USDG/USD Price Feed is available on Arbitrum.

Consistent with the oracle configuration USDG uses on Aave V3 Ethereum Core, Ink, and X Layer, we propose pricing USDG with the Chainlink USDG/USD feed, along with a Capped USDG/USD adapter at a 1.04 price cap.

The final oracle contract, adapter deployment, and configuration remain subject to confirmation by the relevant Aave Risk and Technical Service Providers.

TokenLogic is an active service provider to the Aave DAO, the beneficiary of stream 100086 and the KPI as outlined in this publication. The scope of this engagement is available via this forum proposal.

TokenLogic supports and maintains an independent delegate voting platform within the Aave community.

TokenLogic and associated entities have no undisclosed material conflicts of interest at the time of submission.

  1. Gather feedback from the community.
  2. Using the Direct-to-AIP process, incorporate feedback from the Risk Service Provider and the Technical Service Provider.
  3. Deposit at least $150 worth of USDG into the Aave Short Executor before the market goes live, as required by Aave Governance Framework v2.
  4. Escalate this proposal to the AIP Voting stage.

governance_posts.title: Risk Stewards: JAAA Reserve Parameter Update on Aave V3 Horizon / 2026.10.15
governance_posts.description:
Executive Summary

We propose raising the JAAA reserve-level LTV from 81% to 87% and LT from 86% to 89% on Horizon, while keeping the 5% liquidation bonus. The reserve tier would then sit one percentage point below the JAAA GHO E-Mode, which operates at 88% / 90% / 5%, on both LTV and LT.

The change follows the fund’s settlement record, which Centrifuge has confirmed. Between 10 October 2025 and 5 October 2026, the fund processed 93 redemption orders totalling USD 717.3M across all JAAA vaults. Of these, 91 were paid on the day of the request or the next business day, and the remaining two were paid T+2.

We size the parameters against a three-business-day exit window, one day longer than the slowest settlement observed. Over such a window, the loss a liquidation can carry is the decline in collateral value between seizure and redemption. At 89% LT and a 5% liquidation bonus, the 6.55% solvency margin covers the worst decline of the Palmer Square CLO Senior Debt Index (CLOSE), our stress proxy, over any window of up to six trading days (5.99%), twice the assumed exit window.

The fund’s portfolio has not deteriorated since our original evaluation. Its holdings remain floating-rate AAA CLO tranches, its weighted average legal maturity has shortened with time, and diversification has recovered to 35 positions across 22 managers after the Q1 2026 outflows.

Background

JAAA is the tokenized share class of the Janus Henderson Anemoy AAA CLO Fund, issued through Centrifuge. The fund holds AAA-rated tranches of collateralized loan obligations, and its price on Horizon is derived from the fund NAV, which Chainlink publishes on-chain through the JAAA NAV feed.

Our initial evaluation in December 2025 set the reserve-tier parameters at 81% / 86% / 5%. At that time, redemptions were described as serviced within T+3 with the possibility of longer processing, and the fund had no settlement record under heavy outflows. We therefore sized the LT so that the solvency margin covered the full 8.33% maximum drawdown of CLOSE, which assumes a liquidator may have to hold seized JAAA through an entire sell-off. The 88% / 90% configuration was granted only in the JAAA GHO E-Mode.

Over the past twelve months, the fund has settled more than USD 700M of redemptions, including a single order equal to 43.9% of fund AUM, and Centrifuge has confirmed the settlement times behind them. The exit duration of seized collateral is now supported by an observed settlement record, and we size the reserve-tier parameters against the decline over a three-business-day exit window.

Redemption Settlement

Centrifuge reports the following settlement record from on-chain data across all JAAA vaults, covering 10 October 2025 to 5 October 2026.

Settlement Orders
T+0 63
T+1 28
T+2 2
T+3 or later 0
Total 93 (USD 717.3M)

The largest redemptions in the period were:

  • USD 326.9M on 9 March 2026 (43.9% of fund AUM), priced at the NAV of the request day and paid T+2.
  • USD 300.1M across six orders between 6 and 16 January 2026, each paid T+0 or T+1.
  • USD 200.0M across two orders on 21 and 22 September 2026, on Base and Solana, each paid T+1.

Centrifuge executes redemptions on the day of the request whenever possible, and states that it can redeem USD 300M within T+1. We use T+3 as a conservative exit window in the stress analysis below.

All redemptions settled within 0.5 bps of published NAV on a payout-weighted basis. The March event represents the strongest available real-world stress test. The fund liquidated USD 322.9M par across 18 CLOs at a par-weighted price of 99.87, while AUM fell 61% from USD 1,022M to USD 396M over Q1 2026. Despite this, token NAV rose from 1.0209 to 1.0274.

On 22 and 23 September 2026, the pool manager burned 152.3M shares (USD 160.0M at the published NAV of each day) held by a single address, outside the standard redemption request process.


Source: LlamaRisk, October 15, 2026

Portfolio Composition

We compare the tokenized fund’s own holdings across three snapshots. The first is Particula’s November 2025 rating report, the second is the fund’s holdings in May 2026 after the Q1 outflows, and the third is the holdings table in the fund’s Centrifuge pool metadata.

Metric November 2025 May 2026 September 2026
Fund AUM USD 1,013M USD 409M USD 577M (CLO holdings)
CLO positions 54 20 35
Largest position 3.26% 8.68% 5.20%
Top-10 positions 30.0% 63.8% 37.2%
Distinct CLO managers Not disclosed 13 22
Largest manager Not disclosed 18.6% 12.3%
Weighted average legal final maturity 11.8 years Not disclosed 11.0 years
Share with legal final maturity beyond 12 years 62.2% Not disclosed 30.0%

The holdings remain floating-rate senior CLO tranches, so interest-rate duration stays close to zero. The ETF that follows the same strategy reports an effective duration of 0.04 years, against 0.09 years at the time of our original evaluation.

Weighted average legal final maturity shortened from 11.8 to 11.0 years, in line with the time elapsed between the two snapshots, and the share of holdings maturing beyond 12 years halved. The fund has not extended the maturity profile of its book.

Diversification narrowed during the Q1 2026 outflows, when the fund sold down to 20 positions and the top ten reached 63.8% of holdings. It has since recovered to 35 positions across 22 managers, with the largest position at 5.2% and the top ten at 37.2%. The book remains more concentrated than the 54-position portfolio of November 2025.

The mandate remains AAA CLO tranches, and the ETF reports 99.2% AAA exposure. Two positions totalling 3.5% of holdings are A2 tranches, a class that carries a rating below AAA in some CLO structures, and the holdings table does not show their ratings.

Overall, the portfolio has not deteriorated relative to our original evaluation in interest-rate duration, maturity profile or mandate. Concentration is higher than in November 2025 but well below the May 2026 level.

Stress Analysis

We use CLOSE as the stress benchmark, since the tokenized fund lacks a track record through a credit event of comparable severity. CLOSE tracks senior secured floating-rate CLO debt, the same asset class the fund holds. Over their overlapping history, 7-day returns of the Janus Henderson AAA CLO ETF, which follows the same strategy as the fund, showed a 0.76 correlation and a 0.98 beta to the index. The bounds below use daily CLOSE data from 29 May 2015 to 1 December 2025.

The buffer to LT is the NAV decline that takes a position opened at maximum LTV to liquidation.

\text{Buffer to LT} = 1 - \frac{LTV}{LT}

The solvency margin is the decline, measured from the point a position reaches LT, that collateral can absorb while still covering the debt plus the liquidation bonus.

\text{Solvency margin} = 1 - LT \times (1 + LB)

The margin from entry is the decline a position opened at maximum LTV can absorb before its collateral no longer covers its debt plus the bonus.

\text{Margin from entry} = 1 - LTV \times (1 + LB)

At 87% / 89% / 5%, the buffer to LT is 2.25%, the solvency margin is 6.55%, and the margin from entry is 8.65%.


Source: LlamaRisk, October 15, 2026

A liquidator that seizes JAAA at LT and submits a redemption request the same day carries NAV risk until the redemption is priced. In the March 2026 redemption, the order was priced at the NAV of the request day, which places the price exposure well inside the settlement window. We nonetheless size against the full three-business-day exit window, over which the 5% bonus covers the proxy’s worst decline with a 1.19% margin.

The 8.33% maximum drawdown built up over 27 days. In a decline of that shape, positions cross LT progressively and are liquidated and redeemed within days, so no single liquidation carries the full drawdown. If redemptions were suspended and liquidators could not exit, a position opened at the 87% maximum LTV at the start of the decline would still hold collateral worth more than its debt plus the 5% bonus at the trough, with a 0.32% margin. Redemptions have not been suspended or deferred in any of the fund’s 93 orders.

The token’s own NAV has moved far less than the proxy. Between 23 April and 14 October 2026, the largest daily decline in the Chainlink JAAA NAV feed was 0.07%, and the largest 3-day decline was 0.08%.

Horizon Exposure

JAAA supply on Horizon is $51.9M at a NAV of 1.0522, across eleven addresses. Three positions holding 9,772,596 JAAA (19.8%) use the JAAA GHO E-Mode and are unaffected by this change.

The remaining 39.5M JAAA (80.2%) sit in the reserve tier, where seven positions carry USD 45.0M of debt, of which USD 34.5M is RLUSD and USD 10.5M is GHO. These positions currently borrow 78.2% to 83.4% of their collateral value, close to the current 81% JAAA LTV, which indicates looped positions that are likely to re-lever toward the new limit. At the proposed LT, the health factors of these seven positions rise by 0.023 to 0.038, and the lowest moves from 1.048 to 1.071.

Maximum looped leverage on JAAA rises from 5.26x to 7.69x, following \frac{1}{1 - LTV}. The supply cap bounds the resulting exposure. At the full 60M cap and current NAV, JAAA collateral would be worth USD 63.1M and could support at most USD 54.9M of debt at 87% LTV.

Liquidation Considerations

Restoring a position from LT back to maximum LTV requires a partial liquidation, where x is the debt repaid.

\frac{D_{initial} - x}{C_{initial} - x(1 + LB)} = LTV_{target}

At 87% / 89% / 5%, a liquidator must repay 26.0% of outstanding debt to bring a position from 89% back to 87%, down from 38.9% at the current 81% / 86% / 5%. For the largest reserve-tier position, which carries USD 20.5M of debt, this amounts to about USD 5.3M of RLUSD or GHO.

JAAA is permissioned at the token level, so every liquidator and recipient of seized collateral must be on the fund’s memberlist. A liquidator then exits by redeeming with the fund. The USD 5.3M restoration amount above is small relative to the USD 300.1M the fund redeemed within T+1 in January 2026.

The update carries the following trade-offs:

  • Borrowers gain capital efficiency, with maximum looped leverage rising from 5.26x to 7.69x, and RLUSD and USDC borrowing against JAAA moves to within one percentage point of the GHO E-Mode terms.
  • A position opened at 87% LTV becomes liquidatable after a 2.25% NAV decline, which the proxy exceeded over two trading days in March 2020.
  • The 6.55% solvency margin relies on the fund continuing to settle within three business days. A suspension or deferral of redemptions would leave only the 8.65% margin from entry, which covers the proxy’s maximum drawdown by 0.32%.
  • The largest reserve-tier position holds 38.9% of reserve-tier JAAA, so a single borrower’s management of its position drives most of the liquidation exposure. The new parameters would still allow the borrowers self-manage the positions to rebalance in face of drawdowns, according to historical drawdown velocity.

Recommendation

Based on the fund’s settlement record and the proxy decline over a three-business-day exit window, we recommend updating the JAAA reserve-tier parameters on Horizon as follows:

Configuration LTV LT LB Buffer to LT Margin from entry Max leverage
Reserve, current 81% 86% 5% 5.81% 14.95% 5.26x
Reserve, proposed 87% 89% 5% 2.25% 8.65% 7.69x
E-Mode 10 (JAAA GHO), unchanged 88% 90% 5% 2.22% 7.60% 8.33x

Specification

Asset Parameter Current Recommended
JAAA LTV 81% 87%
JAAA LT 86% 89%
JAAA LB 5% 5%

Next Steps

We will move forward and implement these updates via the Risk Steward process. The implemented changes can be reviewed on the LlamaRisk Risk Stewards Dashboard.

Disclosure

This review was independently prepared by LlamaRisk, a DeFi risk service provider funded in part by the Aave DAO. LlamaRisk is not directly affiliated with the protocol(s) reviewed in this assessment and did not receive any compensation from the protocol(s) or their affiliated entities for this work.

The information provided should not be construed as legal, financial, tax, or professional advice.

Redemption Settlement

Centrifuge reports the following settlement record from on-chain data across all JAAA vaults, covering 10 October 2025 to 5 October 2026.

Settlement Orders
T+0 63

T+3 or later 0
Total 93 (USD 717.3M)

The largest redemptions in the period were:

  • USD 326.9M on 9 March 2026 (43.9% of fund AUM), priced at the NAV of the request day and paid T+2.
  • USD 300.1M across six orders between 6 and 16 January 2026, each paid T+0 or T+1.
  • USD 200.0M across two orders on 21 and 22 September 2026, on Base and Solana, each paid T+1.

Centrifuge executes redemptions on the day of the request whenever possible, and states that it can redeem USD 300M within T+1. We use T+3 as a conservative exit window in the stress analysis below.

All redemptions settled within 0.5 bps of published NAV on a payout-weighted basis. The March event represents the strongest available real-world stress test. The fund liquidated USD 322.9M par across 18 CLOs at a par-weighted price of 99.87, while AUM fell 61% from USD 1,022M to USD 396M over Q1 2026. Despite this, token NAV rose from 1.0209 to 1.0274.

On 22 and 23 September 2026, the pool manager burned 152.3M shares (USD 160.0M at the published NAV of each day) held by a single address, outside the standard redemption request process.


Source: LlamaRisk, October 15, 2026

Portfolio Composition

We compare the tokenized fund’s own holdings across three snapshots. The first is Particula’s November 2025 rating report, the second is the fund’s holdings in May 2026 after the Q1 outflows, and the third is the holdings table in the fund’s Centrifuge pool metadata.

The holdings remain floating-rate senior CLO tranches, so interest-rate duration stays close to zero. The ETF that follows the same strategy reports an effective duration of 0.04 years, against 0.09 years at the time of our original evaluation.

Diversification narrowed during the Q1 2026 outflows, when the fund sold down to 20 positions and the top ten reached 63.8% of holdings. It has since recovered to 35 positions across 22 managers, with the largest position at 5.2% and the top ten at 37.2%. The book remains more concentrated than the 54-position portfolio of November 2025.

The mandate remains AAA CLO tranches, and the ETF reports 99.2% AAA exposure. Two positions totalling 3.5% of holdings are A2 tranches, a class that carries a rating below AAA in some CLO structures, and the holdings table does not show their ratings.

Stress Analysis

We use CLOSE as the stress benchmark, since the tokenized fund lacks a track record through a credit event of comparable severity. CLOSE tracks senior secured floating-rate CLO debt, the same asset class the fund holds. Over their overlapping history, 7-day returns of the Janus Henderson AAA CLO ETF, which follows the same strategy as the fund, showed a 0.76 correlation and a 0.98 beta to the index. The bounds below use daily CLOSE data from 29 May 2015 to 1 December 2025.

The buffer to LT is the NAV decline that takes a position opened at maximum LTV to liquidation.

\text{Buffer to LT} = 1 - \frac{LTV}{LT}

The solvency margin is the decline, measured from the point a position reaches LT, that collateral can absorb while still covering the debt plus the liquidation bonus.

\text{Solvency margin} = 1 - LT \times (1 + LB)

The margin from entry is the decline a position opened at maximum LTV can absorb before its collateral no longer covers its debt plus the bonus.

\text{Margin from entry} = 1 - LTV \times (1 + LB)

At 87% / 89% / 5%, the buffer to LT is 2.25%, the solvency margin is 6.55%, and the margin from entry is 8.65%.


Source: LlamaRisk, October 15, 2026

A liquidator that seizes JAAA at LT and submits a redemption request the same day carries NAV risk until the redemption is priced. In the March 2026 redemption, the order was priced at the NAV of the request day, which places the price exposure well inside the settlement window. We nonetheless size against the full three-business-day exit window, over which the 5% bonus covers the proxy’s worst decline with a 1.19% margin.

The 8.33% maximum drawdown built up over 27 days. In a decline of that shape, positions cross LT progressively and are liquidated and redeemed within days, so no single liquidation carries the full drawdown. If redemptions were suspended and liquidators could not exit, a position opened at the 87% maximum LTV at the start of the decline would still hold collateral worth more than its debt plus the 5% bonus at the trough, with a 0.32% margin. Redemptions have not been suspended or deferred in any of the fund’s 93 orders.

The token’s own NAV has moved far less than the proxy. Between 23 April and 14 October 2026, the largest daily decline in the Chainlink JAAA NAV feed was 0.07%, and the largest 3-day decline was 0.08%.

Horizon Exposure

JAAA supply on Horizon is $51.9M at a NAV of 1.0522, across eleven addresses. Three positions holding 9,772,596 JAAA (19.8%) use the JAAA GHO E-Mode and are unaffected by this change.

The remaining 39.5M JAAA (80.2%) sit in the reserve tier, where seven positions carry USD 45.0M of debt, of which USD 34.5M is RLUSD and USD 10.5M is GHO. These positions currently borrow 78.2% to 83.4% of their collateral value, close to the current 81% JAAA LTV, which indicates looped positions that are likely to re-lever toward the new limit. At the proposed LT, the health factors of these seven positions rise by 0.023 to 0.038, and the lowest moves from 1.048 to 1.071.

Maximum looped leverage on JAAA rises from 5.26x to 7.69x, following \frac{1}{1 - LTV}. The supply cap bounds the resulting exposure. At the full 60M cap and current NAV, JAAA collateral would be worth USD 63.1M and could support at most USD 54.9M of debt at 87% LTV.

Liquidation Considerations

Restoring a position from LT back to maximum LTV requires a partial liquidation, where x is the debt repaid.

\frac{D_{initial} - x}{C_{initial} - x(1 + LB)} = LTV_{target}

At 87% / 89% / 5%, a liquidator must repay 26.0% of outstanding debt to bring a position from 89% back to 87%, down from 38.9% at the current 81% / 86% / 5%. For the largest reserve-tier position, which carries USD 20.5M of debt, this amounts to about USD 5.3M of RLUSD or GHO.

JAAA is permissioned at the token level, so every liquidator and recipient of seized collateral must be on the fund’s memberlist. A liquidator then exits by redeeming with the fund. The USD 5.3M restoration amount above is small relative to the USD 300.1M the fund redeemed within T+1 in January 2026.

The update carries the following trade-offs:

  • Borrowers gain capital efficiency, with maximum looped leverage rising from 5.26x to 7.69x, and RLUSD and USDC borrowing against JAAA moves to within one percentage point of the GHO E-Mode terms.
  • A position opened at 87% LTV becomes liquidatable after a 2.25% NAV decline, which the proxy exceeded over two trading days in March 2020.
  • The 6.55% solvency margin relies on the fund continuing to settle within three business days. A suspension or deferral of redemptions would leave only the 8.65% margin from entry, which covers the proxy’s maximum drawdown by 0.32%.
  • The largest reserve-tier position holds 38.9% of reserve-tier JAAA, so a single borrower’s management of its position drives most of the liquidation exposure. The new parameters would still allow the borrowers self-manage the positions to rebalance in face of drawdowns, according to historical drawdown velocity.

Recommendation

Based on the fund’s settlement record and the proxy decline over a three-business-day exit window, we recommend updating the JAAA reserve-tier parameters on Horizon as follows:

Reserve, proposed 87% 89% 5% 2.25% 8.65% 7.69x

governance_posts.title: Aave DeFi Watcher – Browser Extension for Monitoring Aave Positions
governance_posts.description:
Hi dear aave community :)

I’d like to share Aave DeFi Watcher, a browser extension I built to make monitoring Aave positions simple, fast, and privacy-friendly.

I originally started building it because the previously shared Aave Monitor extension appears to no longer function reliably. For example, many addresses currently return “Failed to fetch” instead of account data. It also only supports Aave V3, while I wanted a tool that could monitor positions across Aave V2, V3, and V4. Since I needed a working solution myself, I decided to build one from scratch.

Features

  • Total Collateral
  • Total Debt
  • Available to Borrow
  • Loan-to-Value (LTV)
  • Liquidation Threshold
  • Health Factor
  • Monitor multiple wallet addresses
  • Support for Aave V2, V3, and V4
  • Support for multiple networks including Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon, and Avalanche
  • Desktop notifications for Health Factor alerts
  • Privacy Mode to hide balances while continuing to monitor your positions
  • Automatic RPC fallback for improved reliability

One of my favorite features is the extension badge, which displays the Health Factor of your selected address directly on the browser toolbar, allowing you to monitor your position at a glance.

The extension is completely read-only. It never asks you to connect a wallet or sign transactions. All account data is fetched directly from Aave’s public smart contracts.

Chrome Web Store

chromewebstore.google.com

Aave DeFi Watcher - Chrome Web Store

Monitor your Aave health factor and liquidation risk in real time across chains.

I built this extension for my own daily use and decided to share it with the community. It’s actively maintained, and I plan to continue adding new features and supporting future Aave releases.

I’d really appreciate any feedback, bug reports or feature suggestions from the community :))

Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, on-chain liquidity, and position health observed in the latest review of Aave V3 reserves.

Aave V3 Core:

  • Reduce supply cap for USDe from 550,000,000 to 400,000,000.
  • Reduce supply cap for sUSDe from 175,000,000 to 130,000,000.
  • Reduce borrow cap for LINK from 1,000,000 to 500,000.

Aave V3 Avalanche:

  • Reduce supply cap for sAVAX from 10,000,000 to 7,000,000.

Aave V3 BNB Chain:

sAVAX(Aave V3 Avalanche)


Source: LlamaRisk, October 15, 2026

The reserve holds 6.73M sAVAX (approximately USD 83.0M) against a 10M supply cap (67.3% utilization). Selling sAVAX into stablecoins incurs a price impact exceeding 2% at approximately USD 210K and reaches the 10% liquidation bonus at approximately USD 783K, which is approximately 0.9% of current deposits. Stablecoin exit liquidity of this size is low relative to the collateral on the reserve, so a liquidation of any material size may not clear profitably through on-chain venues. The proposed cap of 7M sAVAX lands at approximately 96.2% post-change supply cap utilization, limiting further growth of the position until exit liquidity deepens.

Other Cap Reductions


Source: LlamaRisk, October 15, 2026

  • USDe supply on Aave V3 Core reached approximately 785.2M in August and has since declined to 261.4M, a 66.7% reduction from that level and 60.3% over the past 30 days. sUSDe followed the same path, from approximately 366.5M to 104.6M, down 71.5% from its August level and 38.8% over the past 30 days. Stablecoin IRM:

  • Increase Slope1 by 10 bps across V3 stablecoin reserves.

USDC (Aave V3 Monad)

USDC is currently at 90.0% supply cap utilization and 93.5% borrow cap utilization on the Aave V3 Monad instance.

Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, October 13, 2026

The top suppliers hold USDC without outstanding debt. Supply is concentrated, with the largest position accounting for 25.2% of supply, the top three for 51.0%, and the top five for 57.6%.

Borrow Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, October 13, 2026

The top USDC borrowers run health factors between 1.01 and 1.05 with a median of 1.02, and borrowing is concentrated in the largest position. Collateral behind these positions is entirely stablecoin-denominated, with USDe and syrupUSDC the largest by value, syrupUSDC the most widely held, and PT-AUSD-17DEC2026 in a minority of positions.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the supply cap from 250M to 350M and the borrow cap from 225M to 315M on Aave V3 Monad, which places the reserve at approximately 64.3% post-change supply cap utilization and 66.8% post-change borrow cap utilization.

Cap Reductions

  • USDtb on Aave V3 Core sits at 4.3% supply cap utilization and 5.8% borrow cap utilization, with supply down approximately 17% over the past 30 days. The asset is not enabled as collateral, so the reserve serves as a lending market only. The proposed caps of 100M supply and 50M borrow land at approximately 12.9% and 21.2% post-change cap utilization.
  • LDO on Aave V3 Core carries an LTV of 0, so it no longer provides borrowing power for new positions, and borrowing of LDO is disabled. The reserve holds approximately 718.6K LDO against a 2M supply cap (35.9% utilization), reflecting limited adoption. To complete the deprecation of the reserve, the proposed supply cap of 1 closes new deposits, while existing suppliers retain the ability to withdraw and existing positions are otherwise unaffected.
  • tETH on Aave V3 Core sits at 28.7% supply cap utilization, with supply broadly unchanged over the past 30 days, and the asset counts as collateral only within E-Mode. The proposed cap of 300 lands at approximately 95.6% post-change cap utilization.
  • tETH on Aave V3 Prime sits at 69.0% supply cap utilization (15,189 / 22,000). Supply is held within E-Mode as collateral against wstETH debt, in a looped position structure, and is highly concentrated. The proposed cap of 15,000 sits slightly below current outstanding supply.

Stablecoin Slope1 Increases

The recommendation raises Slope1 by 10 BPS, from 4.40% to 4.50%, on stablecoin reserves across Aave V3, and by 5 BPS, from 4.70% to 4.75%, on USDC on Aave V3 Base, continuing the stablecoin interest rate changes proposed by TokenLogic.

governance_posts.description:
Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, position health, and borrow cap headroom observed in the latest review of Aave V3 reserves.

Aave V3 Prime:

  • Increase supply cap for tETH from 15,000 to 20,000.

Aave V3 Core:

  • Reduce supply cap for tETH from 300 to 1.
  • Reduce borrow cap for WBTC from 4,000 to 1,500.
  • Reduce borrow cap for cbBTC from 1,440 to 500.

Aave V3 Arbitrum:

  • Reduce borrow cap for WETH from 135,000 to 75,000.

tETH (Aave V3 Prime and Aave V3 Core)

tETH is listed on both Aave V3 Prime and Aave V3 Core, and on both instances, it counts as collateral only within E-Mode. On Aave V3 Prime, the reserve holds 15,189 tETH (approximately USD 46.9M) against a 15,000 supply cap (101.3% utilization). On Aave V3 Core, supply has remained between approximately 90 and 300 tETH since late April and stands at 286.78 tETH (approximately USD 0.9M), about 1.9% of the Prime figure.

Supply Distribution (Aave V3 Prime)


Source: LlamaRisk, October 16, 2026

The top tETH suppliers have health factors between 1.02 and 1.07 with a median of 1.05, all carry outstanding debt, and supply is highly concentrated, with the largest position accounting for 77.5% of the reserve. Every position borrows wstETH against tETH collateral within the tETH/wstETH E-Mode category, so the health factor of the cohort tracks the tETH/wstETH exchange rate.

Recommendation

Adoption of tETH on Aave V3 Core has remained low, while demand for the asset sits on Aave V3 Prime, where it is paired with wstETH debt in a dedicated E-Mode category. We recommend reducing the supply cap on Aave V3 Core from 300 to 1, which stops new deposits on that instance without affecting existing positions, and raising the supply cap on Aave V3 Prime from 15,000 to 20,000, which places the reserve at approximately 75.9% post-change cap utilization.

Borrow Cap Reductions

  • WBTC on Aave V3 Core carries 700 WBTC of debt (approximately USD 57.3M) against a 4,000 borrow cap (17.5% utilization), with borrows down 10.4% over the past 30 days. The proposed borrow cap of 1,500 lands at approximately 46.7% post-change borrow cap utilization, aligning the cap with observed demand while retaining headroom.
  • cbBTC on Aave V3 Core carries 128 cbBTC of debt (approximately USD 10.5M) against a 1,440 borrow cap (8.9% utilization), with borrows up 24.8% over the past seven days. The proposed borrow cap of 500 lands at approximately 25.7% post-change borrow cap utilization, retaining ample room for further growth.
  • WETH on Aave V3 Arbitrum carries 55,461 WETH of debt (approximately USD 136.0M) against a 135,000 borrow cap (41.1% utilization), with borrows broadly unchanged over the past 30 days. The proposed borrow cap of 75,000 lands at approximately 73.9% post-change borrow cap utilization, aligning the cap with observed demand.

governance_posts.title: [ARFC] Aave V4 Deployment on Tempo
governance_posts.description:
Summary

This ARFC proposes deploying Aave Protocol V4 on Tempo Mainnet.

Motivation

Tempo is a Layer 1 blockchain built for payments. It was incubated by Stripe and Paradigm and is developed in partnership with fintechs and large enterprises including DoorDash, Deel, Shopify and MoneyGram. Tempo is designed for stablecoin use cases including cross-border payments, remittances, embedded finance, payroll and treasury management.

Tempo Mainnet launched on March 18, 2026 and uses chain ID 4217. The network has no native gas token. Transaction fees are paid in USD-denominated stablecoins, with pathUSD used as the default fee token when no other token is specified. Stablecoins on Tempo are issued under the TIP-20 token standard, and the protocol includes an enshrined stablecoin DEX that uses pathUSD as its quote token.

Since launch, the Tempo team has been building yield and credit products with enterprise partners. Deploying Aave V4 on Tempo would make Aave the lending infrastructure available to the enterprises and fintechs building on the network.

The deployment is intended to expand Aave’s liquidity footprint to include traditional enterprises and fintechs, to develop new markets by listing real-world assets available on Tempo, to support stablecoin liquidity growth, and to generate additional protocol revenue for the Aave DAO.

The TEMP CHECK for this deployment passed Snapshot. This ARFC sets out the proposed market scope.

Hub and Spoke Configuration

The proposed initial Tempo deployment will activate with one Liquidity Hub and two Spokes. The Liquidity Hub enables pathUSD and OUSD stablecoins to be borrowed against collateral assets listed in the Main Spoke and RWA Spoke.

Hub Assets
Tempo Core Hub OUSD, cbBTC, PRIME
Hub Spoke Collateral Borrowable
Tempo Core Hub Main Spoke cbBTC, OUSD OUSD
Tempo Core Hub RWA Spoke PRIME OUSD

Other assets may become available before the Aave deployment, and this ARFC may be updated before deployment to include them, subject to risk assessment.

Risk Parameters

The initial token listing and parameters will be updated based on Aave DAO risk service provider analyses.
